brief: The Market Ear curates desk commentary arguing Q3 2026 earnings are less impressive than the headline beat rate suggests. Goldman's David Kostin says earnings growth remains strong but is no longer accelerating, ending the acceleration pattern of recent quarters. FactSet data show median S&P 500 revenue growth slowing from 7.4% in Q1 to 7.2% in Q2 to 7.0% in Q3, with consensus forecasting 6.4% in Q4. Goldman's GIR notes Q3's cumulative EPS surprise running well below the extraordinary beats of Q1 and Q2. Jefferies finds 2026 revenue guidance revisions have turned considerably less positive even as EPS revisions stay strong. Jefferies also flags a brutal asymmetry in which beats draw little excitement but misses, especially in large-cap tech, get punished hard. The real drama has shifted from reported results to increasingly cautious guidance, and the SPX has fallen to 18.4x NTM EPS. Goldman's Tony Pasquariello concludes Q3 will be remembered as a disappointment because several major players missed in their core businesses even though hyperscaler capex intentions are clearly not slowing.
